hints: Focus on the classic test here, alkaline iodine giving a yellow solid is a famous clue for one specific functional group.
The yellow precipitate is triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$, and it only forms when W contains a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group.
Work backwards from the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-$ fragment, it is what is left of W after the $\text{COCH}_3$ part is cut off to make $\text{CHI}_3$.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the iodoform test**

This is the triiodomethane (iodoform) test. A methyl carbonyl compound reacts with alkaline iodine to give a pale yellow precipitate.

General reaction:
$$\text{RCOCH}_3 + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2^- + \text{CHI}_3 + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Identify the yellow precipitate**

The yellow solid is always triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$, not $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$. This immediately narrows the choice to two rows.

Remember, $\text{CHI}_3$ is pale yellow with an antiseptic smell.

**Work backwards to find W**

The other product is the carboxylate ion left behind, here $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-$. So the R group in $\text{RCOCH}_3$ must be $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2$.

That gives:
$$\text{W} = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$$
This is butanone. Propanone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) would give ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2^-$, not propanoate.

options.A: Correct. Butanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$, contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group needed for a positive iodoform test. Cleavage gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-$ plus yellow $\text{CHI}_3$.
options.B: W is correct but the precipitate is wrong. $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ (iodomethane) is a colourless liquid, not a yellow solid. Students sometimes confuse the methyl iodide fragment with triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$.
options.C: Precipitate is correct but W is wrong. Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, does give $\text{CHI}_3$, but the remaining fragment would be ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2^-$, not propanoate $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-$.
options.D: Both parts are wrong for this data. Propanone would not give $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-$, and $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ is never the yellow iodoform precipitate.
